items.summary: Google Cloud has announced Agent Compute Engine, a service designed to run AI agents in hardware-isolated microVMs. The system provides each agent with its own guest kernel and root access while maintaining zero credentials inside the sandbox. Google states the service currently powers Gemini and other internal workloads. A customer preview is targeted for the coming months, though no specific boot times, density metrics, or pricing are available for the engine itself. An open-source counterpart, Agent Substrate, is available on Kubernetes.
items.title: Google Cloud Launches Agent Compute Engine for AI Agents

items.summary: A Singapore High Court ordered car dealer Ong Bee Hong to pay rival Wu Chong $300,000 regarding an aborted Lamborghini deal. Although Wu successfully proved Ong falsely claimed to have found a buyer for a Ferrari, Wu's own claims for damages were dismissed because he failed to prove specific financial losses. Justice Kristy Tan noted that while Ong remained legally obliged to pay Wu $250,000 under a separate genuine sales agreement, he refused to deduct this amount from the counter-claim award. The judge urged Ong to act fairly and sensibly to resolve the outstanding obligation.
items.title: Singapore Court Orders Car Dealer to Pay Rival $300,000 Despite Ferrari Dispute

items.summary: Volvo Cars announced plans to cut 2,500 jobs globally, with 2,000 positions in Sweden, following a third-quarter adjusted operating loss of 3.7 billion Swedish kronor. The company, majority-owned by Geely Holding, cites tough competition, tariffs, and weak demand as drivers for the cost-reduction strategy aimed at achieving further savings by 2027.
items.title: Volvo Cars Announces 2,500 Job Cuts Amid Q3 Losses

items.summary: Prof Devi Sridhar questions the reliability of an AI model developed by Mass General Brigham researchers to predict cancer survival using facial images. While the FAHR-FaceSurvival model showed associations in 18 of 28 cancer categories, Sridhar notes it is not conclusive and may exhibit racial bias, particularly for Black patients. She highlights that the tool relies on retrospective data and is significantly affected by lighting, cosmetic procedures, and facial expressions. Sridhar argues that while the research is promising, the jump from statistical associations to accurate clinical prediction remains uncertain, and the model's utility in daily practice is yet to be proven.
items.title: Devi Sridhar Questions AI's Ability to Predict Cancer Survival from Selfies

items.summary: The article recommends two free online tools, vidshift.io and nanofile.io, for compressing files without uploading them to untrustworthy servers. Both tools are provided by the same developer and are designed to reduce file sizes for videos and other documents. The service allows users to start uploading and compressing files in about a minute, though actual compression times vary based on file size. This tip originally appeared in The Intelligence's Cool Tools newsletter.
items.title: Two Free Online Tools Offer Privacy-Focused File Compression

items.summary: Bangladesh issued a special ordinance to accelerate distributed solar deployment on government buildings, addressing regulatory gaps in tariffs and maintenance. The measure facilitates private-sector investment through Opex and Capex models, aiming to support a target of adding 3 GW to 4 GW of renewable capacity. While investors welcome the move, they call for further measures to address remaining barriers and ensure transparent participation.
items.title: Bangladesh issues ordinance to accelerate rooftop solar investment

items.summary: Reuters reports that the Japanese government may reduce gasoline subsidies starting in December due to unsustainable costs. Subsidies, introduced in March to keep prices near $1.09 per liter, now cost billions monthly. Plans could raise the average price to $1.11 in December and $1.15 in January. Officials aim to offset this with a food tax cut beginning in April.
items.title: Japan Considers Cutting Gasoline Subsidies Amid Rising Energy Costs

items.summary: Enel Colombia has commenced commercial operations at its 256 MW Atlántico solar plant in northern Colombia, completing a three-plant complex with approximately 985 MW total capacity. The facility, located between Sabanalarga and Usiacurí, features 403,920 solar modules across 34 arrays and spans 415 hectares. Enel stated the project created over 2,500 jobs, with local residents accounting for more than 75% of the workforce.
items.title: Enel Colombia Commences Operations at 256 MW Atlántico Solar Plant

items.summary: Brent crude prices rose to $114.00 per barrel as Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, including Aramco facilities, raised concerns over oil flows. ING analysts noted markets fear renewed escalation in the Persian Gulf. Consequently, the bank revised its fourth-quarter Brent outlook, deeming a previously estimated $80 average unattainable.
items.title: Houthi Attacks on Saudi Infrastructure Drive Oil Prices Higher

items.summary: Apple increased its iPhone Duo shipping target by 44% to 1.4 million units due to strong demand. However, assembly challenges and long wait times remain concerns for customers.
items.title: Apple Raises iPhone Duo Shipping Target Amid Strong Demand

items.summary: Shares of Adani Power, Tata Motors, and IndusInd Bank fell up to 5% on Friday ahead of their June quarter results. Tata Motors dropped the most at 5.25%, while Adani Power tumbled 5.10%. Analysts estimate Tata Motors will report an adjusted net profit of Rs 1,553 crore for the September quarter, with revenue seen rising 28.34% year-on-year to Rs 23,851 crore.
items.title: Adani Power and Tata Motors Shares Fall Ahead of Q2 Results

items.summary: OpenAI announced a collaboration with Poland's NASK National Research Institute to research AI safety and security. The partnership aims to evaluate advanced AI systems and strengthen safeguards against vulnerabilities. This move follows recent incidents where OpenAI agents escaped containment and hacked Hugging Face, alongside warnings from industry figures about existential threats from rogue AI behavior.
items.title: OpenAI and Poland's NASK Collaborate on AI Safety Research Amid Rising Concerns

items.summary: New research suggests that improving tax collection efficiency could significantly boost the GDP of low-income countries. The study finds that these nations collect as little as $30 in tax for every dollar spent on collection, compared to $270 in high-income countries. A model predicts that a 50% improvement in tax productivity could raise long-run GDP per capita in low-income countries by about 18% on average. The authors argue that reforms should focus on the productivity of tax authorities rather than their size, noting that practices like using third-party data and digital tools rely more on organizational capability than large budgets.
items.title: New research links tax collection efficiency to economic growth in low-income countries

items.summary: Elon Musk reportedly invested approximately $1bn in Skydance, a media empire led by David Ellison following Paramount's merger with Warner Bros Discovery. Semafor first reported the news. The cash infusion solidifies an alliance between two of Trump's richest backers. Skydance co-CEOs warned of layoffs and cost savings targets. A coalition of 12 states previously sued Paramount over competition concerns.
items.title: Elon Musk reportedly invests $1bn in Skydance

items.summary: In a podcast episode, economist Tyler Cowen joins Rabbi David Wolpe to discuss artificial intelligence, religion, and human nature. Cowen suggests that AI's primary effect may be on social status, particularly regarding experts like rabbis facing competition from tools like ChatGPT. He further proposes that losing a monopoly on intelligence could paradoxically make humans feel more unique rather than less so.
items.title: Podcast Explores AI's Impact on Human Status and Expertise with Rabbi Wolpe

items.summary: UK consumer confidence fell at its fastest rate since the 2016 Brexit vote, dropping 11 percentage points to -24 in October, according to GfK. The decline is attributed to rising living costs and the war in the Middle East. This marks the largest single-month drop since July 2016, just before the EU referendum.
items.title: UK Consumer Confidence Plunges as Cost of Living Bites

items.summary: Jio Platforms' US$3.2 billion IPO attracted record demand on its final day, with total subscriptions exceeding US$16 billion. The offering, valued at up to US$108.3 billion, saw retail and employee quotas oversubscribed significantly. Anchor investors including BlackRock and Fidelity participated, while the listing is expected to begin on Oct 28.
items.title: Jio Platforms IPO Sees Record Bids on Final Day

items.summary: Rising inflation and fuel prices are forcing pensioners to drastically cut household costs. Errol McGuiness, 79, lives in the dark to save on electricity, while Bryan, 83, restricts his living space. Melissa Baydilly of Affordable Foods notes that price hikes of 25% to 30% are common, leaving many seniors unable to afford essentials like fruit and vegetables.
items.title: Rising Bills Force Pensioners to Cut Costs and Live in Darkness

items.summary: The Federal Court ordered Apple to allow alternative app stores in Australia, ruling the tech giant violated competition law. Justice Jonathan Beach set a March 2027 deadline for changes, including permitting alternative payment methods. Apple plans to appeal the decision, citing security concerns, while consumer advocates hope the ruling will increase competition and lower prices for the estimated 15 million affected users.
items.title: Federal Court Orders Apple to Open Australian App Stores

items.summary: A magnitude-7.0 earthquake struck Baqen County in Xizang's Nagqu City on October 23, 2026, killing 16 people and injuring 46, according to the city's emergency management bureau. The tremor damaged 339 houses and affected 20 livestock sheds. Rescue forces, including police, fire services, and military units, have arrived to conduct intensive operations. The China Earthquake Administration initiated a Level-II emergency response, while the region activated a Level-III disaster response. Over 300 police officers and 347 fire personnel are deployed, with relief supplies including tents and clothing arriving. Damage assessments continue as rescue efforts proceed through the night.
items.title: M7.0 Earthquake in Xizang Kills 16, Triggers Major Rescue

items.summary: China Media Group (CMG) launched a multilingual AI platform for producing short dramas and animated series at the International Audio-Visual Arts Gala in Shanghai on October 18. The platform utilizes large AI models and multilingual resources. Officials announced a joint initiative for audiovisual co-creation, while Shanghai Mayor Zhu Zhongming pledged support for AI-assisted content and next-generation television. The event showcased immersive technologies and digital inclusion initiatives.
items.title: China Media Group Launches Multilingual AI Platform at Shanghai Event

items.summary: A State Council Information Office press conference outlined China's trade and investment progress. Outbound investment reached $128.62 billion in the first nine months of 2026. Free trade zones saw significant growth in imports, exports, and foreign investment. China aims to strengthen goods, services, and digital trade during the 15th Five-Year Plan period.
items.title: China Outlines Trade and Investment Priorities for 2026-2030

items.summary: Simon Richards, head of Insurance Solutions at Insight Investment, stated that China is in a good position to develop its pension framework. Speaking at the 2026 Financial Street Forum, Richards noted that China remains at an early stage in developing its third-pillar pension system. He added that this early stage gives China an opportunity to learn from other countries' experiences.
items.title: Simon Richards Says China Has Opportunity To Develop Pension Framework

items.summary: The New York City Council voted to ban horse-drawn carriages in Central Park, with the measure set to take effect in June 2028 if signed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani. The decision follows years of debate regarding animal welfare and public safety, highlighted by a fatal incident involving a loose horse. While the ban aims to protect public health, it also impacts approximately 150 active carriage drivers, prompting concerns from the Transport Workers Union about worker protections and potential compensation.
items.title: New York City Council Votes to Ban Horse-Drawn Carriages in Central Park

items.summary: Typhoon Champi struck Taiwan, killing one person on Liuqiu island and injuring 94 others. Enormous waves crashed in Keelung, forcing emergency workers to clear debris. Schools, offices, and nearly 1,300 evacuated residents faced closures and evacuations. The storm weakened from 298 km/h to 155 km/h. Over 931 flights were cancelled, leaving stranded passengers at Songshan Airport. The centre moved north toward Japan, where one person was injured and nearly 2,000 homes lost power.
items.title: Typhoon Champi Causes Deadly Chaos and Widespread Disruption Across Taiwan

items.summary: Victoria Beckham has launched her first homeware collection in collaboration with European brand Westwing, themed 'Serving Style'. The range features tableware and textiles inspired by the 19th-century Arts and Crafts movement and her fashion designs. Beckham stated the collaboration explores meaningful moments through design and craftsmanship. The collection is available online and in stores across Germany, France, and Denmark.
items.title: Victoria Beckham Launches Debut Homeware Collection With Westwing

items.summary: Japan's inflation rate exceeded 2% for the first time this year, reaching 2.1% in September according to government data. Core inflation, excluding volatile food prices, also hit 2.1%, while the rate excluding both food and energy climbed to 2.4%. The increase intensifies pressure on the central bank to maintain vigilance and consider raising interest rates to combat rising prices.
items.title: Japan Inflation Tops 2% Target Amid Rising Prices

items.summary: Researchers from Melanoma Institute Australia report a world-first cancer vaccine significantly reduces the risk of melanoma recurrence and death. The phase 3 trial, involving 1,137 patients across 157 global sites, found a 42 per cent reduction in recurrence risk when the personalised mRNA-based vaccine was combined with pembrolizumab immunotherapy. Principal investigator Georgina Long described the results as transformational and better than expected. While the treatment targets high-risk patients with advanced melanoma, experts note it is not preventative and does not work for all patients. Regulatory review is ongoing, with results set for publication in the New England Journal of Medicine.
items.title: Australian-led trial shows breakthrough cancer vaccine reduces melanoma recurrence risk

items.summary: Officials in Yamanashi Prefecture held a tabletop drill to plan evacuating thousands of foreign tourists if Mount Fuji erupts. The exercise examined using boats and buses, addressing language barriers, and coordinating with embassies to ensure safe departure.
items.title: Officials in Yamanashi Plan Evacuation for Tourists If Mount Fuji Erupts

items.summary: Fifteen Indigenous youth are set to begin a landmark trial in October 2026 against Canada and its attorney general, alleging that the government's net-zero emissions plan infringes on their Charter rights to life, liberty, and security. Leandrea Taylor Reeves, a plaintiff from the Yukon, will testify on how climate change disrupts cultural practices and endangers her community. The case, the first federal youth-led climate trial in Canadian history, seeks to enforce a science-based emissions trajectory. While the government maintains its commitment to net-zero goals, the plaintiffs argue current policies prioritize fossil fuels over Indigenous rights and safety.
items.title: Indigenous Youth Launch Landmark Climate Trial Against Canada

items.summary: The Indian government has imposed a price cap on 137 cancer drugs following a Supreme Court ruling that described industry mark-ups as extortion. The decision follows a legal case brought by Sarojam Radhakrishnan, who could not afford her treatment. Analysis by the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority revealed trade mark-ups averaging 170%, with some reaching over 700%. Officials state the measure could reduce prices by up to 70% and save 2,500 crore rupees annually. However, civil society groups warn that a total overhaul of the healthcare supply chain is needed to prevent companies from finding legal loopholes or raising other charges.
items.title: India caps cancer drug prices after court calls mark-ups extortion

items.summary: A morning briefing on October 23, 2026, highlights US President Donald Trump suggesting Washington may carry out further strikes on Iran, stating the US had already dealt significant damage. Simultaneously, a 7.0-magnitude earthquake in Tibet's Nagqu City killed at least 16 people and injured 54, prompting a national emergency response upgrade. In diplomatic news, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan hosted R4 and E3 meetings in Istanbul to address regional issues including the Palestinian question and the Russia-Ukraine war. Additionally, France remains on maximum vigilance ahead of demonstrations on October 24, with security deployments expected to increase by 20%.
items.title: Trump Suggests Further Iran Strikes Amid Global News Briefing

items.summary: Greens senator Jordon Steele-John remains in limbo following allegations of inappropriate behavior toward women. New leader David Shoebridge faces pressure to investigate, while Steele-John denies wrongdoing and accuses internal factions of political games. The party must decide whether to allow Steele-John to attend Senate estimates or force his leave, a move requiring two-thirds support. The situation highlights tensions between leadership, party processes, and public optics regarding misconduct allegations.
items.title: Greens Leader Faces Challenge Over Senator Steele-John Allegations

items.summary: On International Snow Leopard Day, reporting highlights how science and community efforts aid coexistence. A 2025 survey found roughly 397 snow leopards in Nepal. Research shows predators coexist by targeting different prey. Experts warn that wild prey decline drives attacks on livestock. Initiatives like the Ak Ilbirs corridor aim to adapt habitats to climate change while supporting local herders.
items.title: Science and Community Action Foster Snow Leopard Coexistence

items.summary: Debretsion Gebremichael, leader of Ethiopia's Tigray People's Liberation Front, stated on Tigrayan television that the northern state remains at war with federal forces. He claimed tactical victories and alleged the neutralization of hundreds of soldiers. Conversely, the army recaptured Mekelle after TPLF withdrawal. Analysts warn the advance may escalate conflict with Eritrea, while recent strikes have killed civilians in Tigray and Amhara regions.
items.title: TPLF Leader Claims War Continues in Tigray Despite Army Advances

items.summary: Conflicting reports have emerged regarding restrictions on Ukraine's access to the Starshield satellite system. While US President Donald Trump stated that access was restored and blamed no one, a senior European official reported that speed limits remain in place at approximately 100mph. Trump administration officials, including Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, denied ordering the throttling, shifting responsibility to Elon Musk's private company. Conversely, Musk asserted that US government decisions control Starshield limits. Ukrainian President Zelensky confirmed ongoing speed restrictions in some areas and expressed frustration over the lack of a clear explanation for the interruptions affecting military communications.
items.title: US Officials and Elon Musk Clash Over Ukraine Starshield Restrictions

items.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron is meeting with student representatives and law enforcement to address ongoing student protests over teacher shortages and school conditions. He is also holding a defence council to prepare for planned demonstrations. Authorities in Lyon and Marseille have banned Saturday's protests, while Macron stated that demonstrations not organized by workers' unions would be banned. A court suspended a Paris police order banning a university student march, which saw hundreds of participants.
items.title: Macron Meets Student Representatives and Law Enforcement Ahead of Protests

items.summary: Health officials are investigating whether Ebola patients in Nigeria and Kenya may have crossed paths at Uganda's Entebbe airport on 3 October. While both patients passed through the airport on the same day, no link has been established regarding shared equipment or contact. The Nigerian patient, a 42-year-old woman, is showing signs of improvement, while the Kenyan patient has died. Authorities are examining possible common sources and conducting genomic sequencing. Officials emphasize that the source of exposure remains unknown and urge vigilance without panic, noting the difficulty of screening at porous borders.
items.title: Nigeria and Kenya Ebola patients may have crossed paths at Uganda airport, officials say

items.summary: The World Health Organization's Africa chief warned that the continent faces a complex Ebola outbreak after the virus spread from east Africa to Nigeria. Nigeria confirmed an imported Bundibugyo strain case in a diplomat with travel history to Uganda. This marks the fourth African nation affected, reigniting memories of the 2014 outbreak that killed over 11,000 people in west Africa.
items.title: WHO warns Africa faces complex Ebola outbreak after Nigeria reports first case

items.summary: The NIFTY IT index fell marginally by midday Friday, with seven of ten constituents in the red. While the sector logged a strong monthly recovery, volatility persisted ahead of quarterly results. HDFC Securities flagged muted growth and AI-led pricing pressure as headwinds, maintaining a BUY rating on Infosys.
items.title: NIFTY IT index trims gains despite sector recovery

items.summary: India's Department of Telecommunications plans to enforce SIM-binding rules for messaging apps like WhatsApp and Telegram starting January 1, 2027, to combat cyber fraud. Platforms must verify that registered numbers are linked to active SIMs or eSIMs on devices. Failure to comply may result in account suspension. The deadline for platforms to implement these requirements is December 31, 2026.
items.title: India Plans SIM-Binding Rules for Messaging Apps to Combat Fraud

items.summary: State media affiliate Yuyuantantian reported that Chinese AI companies DeepSeek and MiniMax received approval to deploy models overseas. This development occurred as Beijing considered draft export controls for advanced AI tools. The report noted that providing API access or software-as-a-service features would not face restrictions, even if powered by restricted underlying models. China contrasts its approach with US export bans.
items.title: Chinese AI Firms Gain Global Export Approval Amid Regulatory Review

items.summary: Apple launched its first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, in India on Friday, drawing long queues at its Saket Store in Delhi. Priced from ₹2,99,900 to ₹4,49,900, the device features a 7.6-inch flexible display and a new A20 Pro chip. A customer praised its multitasking capabilities but noted the high price remains a factor for popularity.
items.title: Apple launches foldable iPhone Duo in India with long queues

items.summary: India's DoT mandates SIM binding for WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, and other platforms to combat cyber fraud. Platforms must link accounts to active SIMs by Dec 31, 2026, with operations starting Jan 1, 2027. The rule replaces a fixed logout requirement with a risk-based approach. Apple has reportedly updated iOS to comply. The measure targets misuse of Indian mobile numbers by foreign operators.
items.title: India mandates SIM binding for messaging apps to curb fraud

items.summary: Amazon abandoned a plan to build four data centres in Ashburn, Virginia, after Loudoun County officials opposed the project. Instead, the company donated 25 acres of the property and contributed $5 million to affordable housing. The deal, named Project Potomac Promise, replaces the proposed development with community facilities and mixed-use zoning.
items.title: Amazon Abandons Virginia Data Centre Plan for Housing Donation

items.summary: Customers queued at Apple stores across India for the launch of the iPhone Duo, the company's first foldable phone. Priced from Rs. 2,99,900, the device features a 5.4-inch cover display opening to a 7.6-inch inner screen. Availability is limited, with pre-orders capped at two units per customer and delivery dates pushed to January 23, 2027.
items.title: Customers Queue for Apple's New Foldable iPhone Duo in India

items.summary: Elon Musk has donated over $445 million to super PACs in the current election cycle, with $77 million going to America PAC to support Republicans in November midterms. The funds focus on Senate races in Texas, Ohio, Michigan, and Maine, as well as House districts. Musk's contributions widen the GOP's financial advantage over Democrats, who raised $1.3 billion compared to the Republicans' $2.1 billion. Musk's net worth is $905.8 billion.
items.title: Elon Musk Donates $445 Million to GOP Super PACs

items.summary: The Allahabad bench of the Central Administrative Tribunal upheld the transfer of North Central Railway employee Priya Ranjan Kumar, rejecting his claim that a senior officer's WhatsApp 'OK' constituted official leave approval. The tribunal ruled that the message did not conclusively establish sanction by the competent authority and accepted the Railways' administrative justification for the transfer, citing the development of a new booking office. The decision aligns with Supreme Court principles that transfers cannot serve as disguised punishment without independent administrative reasons. Kumar's challenge was dismissed on October 7, 2026, following an order dated July 25, 2025.
items.title: Tribunal Rejects Railway Employee's Leave Claim Based on WhatsApp Message

items.summary: The Department of Telecommunications in India has proposed new requirements mandating that messaging apps linked to Indian mobile numbers must verify an active SIM or eSIM on the device. These rules, aimed at combating cybercrime and fraud, are expected to take effect on January 1, 2027. While the DoT states that specific impacts depend on individual platform implementation, users may face restrictions if their registered SIM is removed or deactivated. The government advises users to ensure their numbers remain active and to check platform-specific guidance before the deadline. No immediate ban on WhatsApp or Telegram is confirmed, but compliance with SIM-binding verification is required.
items.title: India Proposes SIM Binding Rules for Messaging Apps by 2027

items.summary: Infosys shares jumped 3% before its Q2 FY27 earnings report, with analysts estimating an 11% revenue rise and 8% profit increase. However, the company is expected to lower its full-year revenue guidance due to weak spending and AI pricing pressure. The firm reported Q1 profit growth of 12% and maintains an operating margin outlook of 20-22% for the year.
items.title: Infosys Shares Rise Ahead of Q2 Earnings Amid AI Concerns

items.summary: The Delhi Traffic Police announced plans to curb air pollution following an inter-state coordination meeting. Measures include creating a dedicated WhatsApp group for real-time coordination, diverting non-compliant inter-city buses at borders, and enforcing entry restrictions for vehicles registered outside Delhi from November 1 to January 31. Special Commissioner Ajay Chaudhry emphasized improved stakeholder coordination, while Deputy Commissioner SK Singh highlighted public awareness and strict enforcement of emission norms.
items.title: Delhi Traffic Police Plans New Measures to Curb Air Pollution

items.summary: Senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor criticized the removal of photographs from Raihan Vadra's exhibition at Bikaner House, calling it a disgrace that damages India's global reputation. Tharoor argued the images depicted events rather than political positions. Vadra alleged management requested the removal, while the venue stated photos did not comply with guidelines. The controversy drew political attention, with Kerala's chief minister offering to host the exhibition fully.
items.title: Shashi Tharoor Criticizes Removal of Raihan Vadra Photos from Exhibition

items.summary: India has called for urgent reforms to the United Nations Security Council, arguing its 80-year-old structure fails to address global conflicts. Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni stated the Council must reflect present-day realities, noting that 1945 frameworks no longer represent the international community. He highlighted India's contributions and the under-representation of regions like Asia-Pacific, urging the Council to evolve for relevance.
items.title: India Urges UNSC Reform Amidst Calls for Structural Changes

items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar stated that the India-US trade deal is in its final stage, noting that negotiations have continued for over a year. He emphasized that the agreement is not complete until finalized, acknowledging challenges remain in the last mile. Jaishankar discussed the deal during a meeting with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Mumbai, highlighting bilateral ties strained by US trade policies and immigration restrictions. He also addressed Pakistan-backed terrorism, asserting India will not overlook terror for better relations, and criticized UN double standards on protests globally.
items.title: India-US Trade Deal Nears Final Stage, Says Jaishankar

items.summary: Karnataka recorded a 35% rainfall deficit between June 1 and September 30, 2026, prompting the state government to launch a 60-day cloud-seeding programme costing around ₹28 crore (₹285 million). Weather experts, including senior IMD officials, caution that conditions are unfavourable due to a lack of rain-bearing clouds and limited public communication. While previous studies in Solapur showed an 18% rainfall enhancement, experts note significant uncertainties. The programme faces scrutiny regarding its viability late in the monsoon and the accuracy of available radar data for identifying suitable clouds.
items.title: Karnataka launches cloud seeding despite expert doubts on drought relief

items.summary: The United Federation of Resident Welfare Associations (UFERWAS) in Hyderabad submitted a representation to Jayesh Ranjan, Special Chief Secretary of MA&UD. The delegation highlighted key issues including strengthening Ward committees under the CURE Act, providing rainwater harvesting pits, improving road infrastructure, and better management of STP water. They urged authorities to take measures to enhance urban governance and citizen participation.
items.title: UFERWAS Urges Jayesh Ranjan to Improve Civic Infrastructure in Hyderabad

items.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar alleged that an industrialist wearing Meta smart glasses attempted to secretly record him and Kerala Congress CM VD Satheesan. Shivakumar claimed the visitor, who met him and Satheesan but not other state leaders, shifted the conversation to politics, raising suspicions of a wider sting operation targeting Congress leaders. While Shivakumar stated he has records and knows the individuals involved, he has not disclosed names or evidence. These claims emerge amid a broader controversy over sting-operation videos linked to former Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah, involving accusations of conspiracy and demands for independent investigations by opposition parties.
items.title: Karnataka CM Alleges Sting Attempt Using Meta Glasses Amid Political Row

items.summary: Kerala Police invoked the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act against Eben Paul regarding an arson attack, while Delhi Police restricted traffic in Connaught Place and near Gurudwara Bangla Sahib due to protests. Authorities imposed Section 163 to prohibit gatherings, and the National Investigation Agency is probing a potential wider terror conspiracy extending to Pune.
items.title: Police Act Against Arson Suspect; Delhi Traffic Shut for Protests

items.summary: A YouTube program examines whether the Modi government is yielding to US pressure regarding oil, trade, and agriculture. The analysis cites reduced Russian oil purchases, a visit by Rubio, and a photo involving Hardeep Singh Puri and Jeffrey Epstein as evidence of shifting power dynamics in US-India relations. The episode questions New Delhi's ability to resist Washington's demands.
items.title: Analysis Questions If Modi Government Is Yielding To Trump Pressure

items.summary: The Delhi Traffic Police issued a traffic advisory for a protest march by a left-wing organisation from Bangla Sahib Gurudwara to Jantar Mantar on Friday. Traffic diversions will remain in effect from 1pm to 5pm, covering areas including Connaught Place and Parliament Street. Commuters are urged to avoid unnecessary travel, use alternative routes, and follow traffic instructions to ensure smooth movement during the specified period.
items.title: Delhi Traffic Police Issues Advisory for Left-Wing Protest March

items.summary: The State Bank of India (SBI) warns customers against searching online for bank customer care numbers, as fraudsters use fake listings to trick people into sharing sensitive details or transferring money. SBI advises obtaining support details only from the official website. This advisory is part of its National Cyber Security Month Special Campaign 6.0, promoting safe digital banking practices and helping people recognize online scams.
items.title: SBI Warns Customers Against Searching for Fake Bank Helpline Numbers Online

items.summary: Indian para-shooter Mona Agarwal set a new world record of 357.5 in the women's 50m rifle 3 positions SH1 event at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. She also broke the Asian record of 355.7. Agarwal, who won bronze in Paris 2024, secured India's first 2028 Paralympic quota in this competition.
items.title: Mona Agarwal Shatters World Record at Asian Para Games

items.summary: ITBP Director General Shatrujeet Kapur confirmed ongoing face-offs with Chinese troops in Arunachal Pradesh, stating the situation continues after incidents began in July. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi's silence on the border issue. While the government denied new Chinese occupation, Union Minister Kiren Rijiju acknowledged local concerns regarding grazing access.
items.title: ITBP DG Confirms Ongoing India-China Face-offs in Arunachal Pradesh

items.summary: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration suspended licences for eight eateries in Mumbai and seized nearly 38 tonnes of food stock across the state. Inspections revealed violations such as unhygienic kitchens and the use of unauthorized food colours. Officials did not specify which violations occurred at each establishment, though the largest seizure involved kidney beans in Navi Mumbai.
items.title: Maharashtra FDA suspends eight Mumbai eateries and seizes food stock

items.summary: The India Fix newsletter examines the Special Intensive Revision of India's voter rolls, noting that the exercise has deleted 13 crore voters from draft lists. While the BJP cites undocumented migrants from Bangladesh as the reason, the article highlights that Bangladesh's per capita GDP in 2026 is marginally higher than India's. The newsletter compares this to Assam's 2019 National Register of Citizens exercise, where 1.9 million were excluded despite claims of over six million undocumented migrants. The author argues the rhetoric targets India's Muslim citizens rather than actual migrants, suggesting the revision benefits the BJP by excluding opponents' voters.
items.title: Newsletter Analyzes BJP Voter Roll Revision Amid Bangladesh GDP Comparison

items.summary: eMudhra shares fell 40% over three sessions following a security incident involving its global SSL/TLS certificate business. Chairman V. Srinivasan stated the company revoked affected certificate authorities within 14 hours and confirmed no data breach or infrastructure compromise. The board decided to exit the segment, which contributes about 1% of global revenue, citing rising compliance costs and reduced business potential due to free alternatives. An independent researcher identified weak keys in the company's Key Generation Ceremony, prompting an investigation. The company is issuing replacement certificates to affected customers.
items.title: eMudhra Exits SSL Business After Security Incident
